title: Signals event (schema_version 1)
description: One event object as emitted by a Signals SDK and carried in a batch envelope (see batch.schema.json). The envelope keys are closed (`additionalProperties: false`); an unknown envelope key rejects the single event with reason `schema`. Keys inside `attrs` are open and preserved by collectors. Serialised-size caps (16 KB per event, 2 KB `args`, 4 KB `fields`, 8 KB `props`) cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by collectors with reason `too_large`. Length caps on strings are expressed as `maxLength` and count Unicode code points.

id.description: UUIDv7 generated by the SDK. Together with `ts` and the collector's project it forms the idempotency key `(project, ts, id)`. Hex digits may be either case; collectors compare case-insensitively.

ts.description: Event time on the SDK clock as an RFC 3339 date-time. Never clamped or rewritten by anyone; collectors use the literal string as part of the idempotency key. SDKs MUST emit the canonical form `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ` (UTC, exactly millisecond precision); collectors must accept this form and may reject other RFC 3339 forms with schema. The reference mock accepts parseable RFC 3339 forms but rejects leap seconds at the schema-validation step. For events carrying `duration_ms` this is the start of the measured interval, except `session.ended`, whose `ts` is the moment the session ended.

session_id.description: MCP session id when the transport has one, otherwise an SDK-synthesised id. Optional; when present, a non-empty string of at most 256 code points.

attrs.description: Type-specific attributes; the shape is selected by `type` (see $defs). Unknown keys are preserved.

$comment: Events may nest at most 128 object/array levels, counting the event object as level 1; collectors enforce deeper values as schema rejections before sizing.

event_type.description: Closed set of event types. Any other value is rejected with reason `unknown_type`.

client.description: The MCP client as learned from the `initialize` request. Optional; every key is optional (partial is fine). No other keys are allowed. Caps (code points): `name` 128, `version` 64, `protocol_version` 32; an SDK truncates to them before the event cap check (CONTRACT.md §6).

caller.description: Who called the server. Optional; every key is optional (partial is fine) and may be null. No other keys are allowed. `key_id` comes from the trusted `X-Signals-Caller` header, `subject` from an access token, `ip` is the raw address as seen by the server (the collector hashes it and never stores the raw value). Caps (code points): `key_id` 128, `subject` 256, `user_agent` 512; an SDK truncates to them before the event cap check (CONTRACT.md §6). `key_id`, `subject` and `user_agent` are set only when the resolved value is already a string: a non-string claim or header value is ignored and the key omitted, never coerced, because coercion would run caller code (CONTRACT.md §3 and §6 "Caller-supplied values"). A value here that is neither a string nor null rejects the event with reason `schema`.

subject_kind.description: How the server established `subject` (contract 1.1.0, CONTRACT.md §3): `oauth` a validated access-token claim, `api_key` a credential the server itself verified, `header` a value a trusted proxy supplied, `none` the server has no subject identity. Optional and, like every other `caller` value, may be null. Collectors use it to rank identity strength; `oauth` is the only strong kind. When it is `none`, `subject` must be absent or null (enforced below).

then.description: `subject_kind: none` means the server resolved no subject, so a subject value here would contradict it.

byte_count.description: A size in bytes of a compact (no whitespace) UTF-8 JSON serialisation; 0 when the counted field is absent or no response was sent. Counting rule (CONTRACT.md §4): the exact size of the compact JSON serialisation of the payload value, computed from the wire text or by a serialisation-equivalent walk; when that walk stopped at the SDK's budget (§6 Counting budgets: at least 100 000 visited nodes or 1 MiB) the field is the count reached, a lower bound; 0 only when the platform's reference serialiser can produce no form for the entire input (a cycle, or in JavaScript a BigInt, for which JSON.stringify throws on the whole value). An unsupported member never zeroes the value that contains it: the member contributes nothing and its siblings are counted exactly (CONTRACT.md §6 "Conditions: capture and counting").

item_count.description: A count of items, never bytes (contract 1.1.0).

char_count.description: A count of Unicode code points of text content, excluding binary blobs (contract 1.1.0, CONTRACT.md §4 "Context-cost fields"). Follows the same budget rule as `byte_count`: when the SDK's walk stopped at its counting budget the field is the count reached, a lower bound.

error_kind.description: What kind of failure the SDK observed (contract 1.1.0, CONTRACT.md §4 "Error classification"). Closed set, first match in the §4 precedence order wins: `cancelled` (the request was cancelled and no response was sent), `timeout` (a deadline expired), `auth` (rejected before the handler ran for authentication or authorisation), `unknown_tool` (the named tool, prompt or resource is not advertised), `invalid_params` (a known target whose parameters were rejected), `protocol` (any other JSON-RPC protocol error), `internal` (the handler or server raised an unexpected exception), `tool` (the handler returned a result with `isError: true`). The key is omitted -- never set to a placeholder -- when the SDK cannot classify the failure; a collector reads an absent `error_kind` on an `is_error` event as "unknown kind".

error_code.description: The JSON-RPC `error.code` of the response, when there was one (contract 1.1.0). Any integer, including the negative reserved range (`-32700`, `-32600`, `-32601`, `-32602`, `-32603`); omitted when the failure produced no JSON-RPC error object.

request_id.description: The JSON-RPC `id` of the request this event reports, so cancellations, progress notifications and the call can be joined (contract 1.1.0). A string id is used as it arrived, truncated to 64 code points; a number id is its decimal form; an absent, null or otherwise typed id means the key is omitted. Scoped to one session, not globally unique.

content_hash.description: A digest an SDK computes over content it observed, as lower-case hexadecimal (contract 1.1.0, CONTRACT.md §4 "Catalogue hashes"). Opaque to collectors: they may test two hashes for equality but never parse one, and never compare hashes across different `source.sdk` values. It must be a pure function of the content, independent of iteration order, of the event's truncation state and of process identity.

error_kind_consistency.description: CONTRACT.md §4 "Error classification": `is_error` is true whenever `error_kind` is present, with one exception -- `error_kind: cancelled`, where no response was sent at all and `is_error` is false. Both directions are enforced (contract 1.1.0, review round 1, S1): an event that names a kind other than `cancelled` while reporting success is rejected with reason `schema`, and so is one that names `cancelled` while reporting a failure. `tool.called` adds that `error_kind: cancelled` requires `cancelled: true`.

tool_entry.description: One advertised tool in a `tools.listed` snapshot (contract 1.1.0). `name` is the tool name as advertised and is the only required key: the snapshot carries names, annotation keys and hashes, never a schema, a description or a result. `annotations` lists the distinct annotation hints whose value is true, with the `Hint` suffix removed (`destructiveHint: true` -> `destructive`); `title` is never included. `schema_hash` is a digest of the tool's advertised `inputSchema`. The SDK fits the 16 KB event cap by dropping `annotations`, then `schema_hash`, then whole entries (CONTRACT.md §6 "Event cap").

truncated_object.description: The only permitted replacement object inside `args`, `fields` or `props`: exactly `{"_truncated": true, "_bytes": <int >= 0>}`. It stands for the whole field when the field is still over its serialised-size cap after redaction (CONTRACT.md §6), and for one member the SDK may not serialise -- a subtree deeper than the capture cap, or an unsupported member (CONTRACT.md §6 "Conditions: capture and counting") -- whose siblings are still captured and counted exactly. `_bytes` is the serialised size of what the marker replaced, for the whole-field case the redacted object that was dropped and never the pre-redaction size, and follows the counting rule of CONTRACT.md §4: the exact compact serialised size, the count reached when the walk stopped at the SDK's budget, and 0 only when that value has no serialisable form at all. A field-cap overflow is a budget condition, not a serialisation failure: the size is exact for the redacted copy even when that copy carries a per-member marker inside it. For a cycle, capture marks the back-edge at the cycling member's own position and preserves its siblings; the SDK may choose this standard marker object with `_bytes`: 0 or a short string marker such as "[cycle]". Both cycle marker forms conform, and counting remains 0 for the whole input (CONTRACT.md §6). A shared object is expanded at most once in one capture, so capture is not required to be path-relative: a marker may sit where the *first* path that reached the value found a back-edge, even where a later path to the same value would not have cut there (CONTRACT.md §6). Any object carrying a `_truncated` key must have exactly this shape; the SDK renames caller-owned top-level `_truncated` / `_bytes` keys to `_truncated_user` / `_bytes_user` before emitting, appending a further `_user` while the name is taken (`_truncated_user_user`, …). For a property key longer than the serialised-byte budget, the SDK must not allocate in proportion to the key: its length may be read, but its contents must not be normalised, copied, sliced, re-encoded or otherwise traversed, including for redaction, Unicode repair or reserved-key renaming (the 1.0.14 length-only oversized input chunk discipline). The captured member must not carry caller key bytes, and siblings must be captured exactly, including replacement-name collisions. One over-long key must not replace the whole field unless the resulting captured copy is still over the field cap; then _bytes is its exact serialised size, including the replacement entry. Counting reports the count reached, a lower bound, and must still reach at least 100 000 visited nodes or 1 MiB of serialised output before stopping; an over-long key must not short-circuit that minimum. The exact form of the replacement entry is the SDK's choice subject to these requirements; conformance tests must assert these properties rather than a particular literal (CONTRACT.md §6).

session.started.description: A session began. `ts` is no later than any other event in this session; for a synthetic session it equals the start of the request that created it. `transport` names the real transport (`stdio`: one session per process; `sse`: legacy SSE with a session id; `streamable-http`: Streamable HTTP with a session id); `synthetic` when the SDK synthesised the session, which happens for stateless Streamable HTTP and in the documented late-instrumentation degraded mode (CONTRACT.md §6). When several events of one session share a `ts`, `session.started` sorts before the others.

derived.description: True when the SDK synthesised this session's identity from caller attributes and an idle window instead of observing one from the transport's own session management (contract 1.1.0, CONTRACT.md §4). In `schema_version` 1 that is exactly the `transport: synthetic` case, so the two must agree and the schema enforces it; the key exists so a collector can label derived sessions without re-reading `transport`, and so a later protocol revision that hands the SDK a nameable transport without a session id can keep the flag unchanged.

session.ended.description: A session ended. `ts` is the moment the session ended (not its start); `duration_ms` gives its length.

mcp.initialize.description: The MCP `initialize` handshake. Only the top-level capability keys are reported, never their values. `duration_ms`, `is_error` and `error_kind` are optional (contract 1.1.0) so handshake success can be measured; an SDK that cannot time the handshake omits them.

client_capabilities.description: Top-level keys of the client's `capabilities` object: at most 32 keys of at most 64 code points each. An SDK truncates (drops keys from the end, keeping the prefix) rather than dropping the event.

server_capabilities.description: Top-level keys of the server's `capabilities` object: at most 32 keys of at most 64 code points each. An SDK truncates (drops keys from the end, keeping the prefix) rather than dropping the event.

tool.called.description: A `tools/call` request completed, failed or was cancelled. `args` is present only when argument capture is on; it is redacted and capped at 2 KB serialised (collector reason `too_large` when over).

input_schema_valid.description: Whether the call's arguments satisfied the tool's declared `inputSchema` (contract 1.1.0). Absent -- never a placeholder -- when the SDK could not evaluate it: no schema was declared, no validator was available, or validation was skipped. False normally accompanies `is_error: true` with `error_kind: invalid_params`, but the two are independent observations.

output_schema_valid.description: Whether the result's `structuredContent` satisfied the tool's declared `outputSchema` (contract 1.1.0). Absent when the tool declares no `outputSchema` or the SDK could not evaluate it.

progress_events.description: How many `notifications/progress` the server sent for this call (contract 1.1.0). Emitted only when `SIGNALS_PROTOCOL_EVENTS` is on (CONTRACT.md §6).

first_progress_ms.description: Milliseconds from the start of the call to its first `notifications/progress` (contract 1.1.0); absent when no progress notification was sent. Emitted only when `SIGNALS_PROTOCOL_EVENTS` is on.

output_kinds.description: Distinct `content[].type` values of the result in first-appearance order; `resource_link` maps to `resource`; `ui` when the tool is a UI tool (detected from the registered tool's or the result's `_meta["ui/resourceUri"]`).

cancelled.description: True when the call was cancelled by `notifications/cancelled` before a response was sent; then `is_error` is false, `output_bytes` is 0 and `output_kinds` is empty (enforced by `if`/`then` below).

args.description: Redacted tool arguments (shared key policy, recursive). At most 2 KB (2048 bytes) serialised; enforced by collectors as `too_large`. When still over the cap after redaction the SDK sends the `truncated_object` marker `{"_truncated": true, "_bytes": <serialised size after redaction>}` instead; an object carrying `_truncated` must be exactly that marker. Top-level `_truncated` / `_bytes` are reserved for the marker: caller-owned keys of those names are renamed to `_truncated_user` / `_bytes_user`, with a further `_user` appended while the name is taken (CONTRACT.md §4).

then.description: A cancelled call got no response: no error, no output, and no error kind other than `cancelled`.
Only a cancelled call can report the `cancelled` kind (contract 1.1.0, review round 1, S1): on `tool.called` the two must agree in both directions.

prompt.get.description: A `prompts/get` request completed. `output_bytes` is the serialised size of `result.messages` (or of the JSON-RPC `error` object).

mcp.request.description: Any other MCP request that received a response (`tools/list`, `ping`, `completion/complete`, ...). Subject to `SIGNALS_SAMPLE_REQUESTS`. Notifications are not reported.

tools.listed.description: A snapshot of the tool catalogue the server advertises (contract 1.1.0). The session's catalogue is emitted once, on the first `tools/list` that succeeded, and again on every `notifications/tools/list_changed`; a failed `tools/list` emits an `is_error: true` snapshot that carries no catalogue and does not consume that one emission, so a session may carry both (review round 1, B2). it does not replace the `mcp.request` event for `tools/list`, which is still reported subject to `SIGNALS_SAMPLE_REQUESTS`. Every attribute is optional: an SDK reports what it can observe. The snapshot carries names, annotation keys and hashes only -- never a schema, a description or a result. `count` is the number of tools advertised and is never reduced by truncation, so `count` greater than the length of `tools` means entries were dropped to fit the 16 KB event cap and `truncated` is true (CONTRACT.md §6 "Event cap").

count.description: How many tools the server advertised at this snapshot, before any truncation. It is the advertised total even when `tools` is shorter or absent.

tools.description: The advertised tools, at most 500 entries. Order is the order the server advertised them. An SDK with more than 500 advertised tools keeps the first 500 and sets `truncated`.

truncated.description: True when this snapshot is incomplete because the SDK shrank it to fit the 16 KB event cap or the 500-entry cap: annotations dropped, `schema_hash` dropped, or whole entries dropped. The retained entry count is the length of `tools`; `count` and `catalog_hash` still describe the full catalogue.

catalog_hash.description: A digest over the full advertised catalogue, computed before any truncation, so it changes when and only when the catalogue changes (CONTRACT.md §4 "Catalogue hashes").

is_error.description: True when the `tools/list` request this snapshot came from failed. `count`, `tools` and `catalog_hash` are then absent (enforced below) because nothing was advertised, and the snapshot does not consume the session's one catalogue emission: the first later success still emits it.

source.description: What produced the snapshot: `list` the session's catalogue, taken from the first `tools/list` that succeeded, `list_changed` a `notifications/tools/list_changed` the server sent.

then.description: A failed `tools/list` advertised nothing, so a failed snapshot carries no catalogue: `count`, `tools` and `catalog_hash` must all be absent (contract 1.1.0, review round 1, S2). `count: 0` with `is_error: false` is the empty-catalogue success and is a different fact.

log.description: A log line from `signals.log()` or a logging bridge. `fields` is redacted and capped at 4 KB (4096 bytes) serialised; enforced by collectors as `too_large`. `tool` is set when emitted inside a tool handler. A logging integration handed a caller-owned string chunk decides whether that chunk is oversized from its length alone, before any iteration, indexing, slicing, regular expression, decoding or other character access, against the serialised-byte budget of CONTRACT.md §6. An oversized chunk yields bounded telemetry naming the drop and the chunk's length -- never silence -- and its contents are never inspected, parsed, copied or retained, so records embedded in it are not recovered; a chunk under the threshold is handled normally, preserving several records in one chunk and the records adjacent to a large one.

fields.description: Structured fields, redacted with the shared key policy (recursive). At most 4 KB (4096 bytes) serialised; enforced by collectors as `too_large`. When still over the cap after redaction the SDK sends the `truncated_object` marker `{"_truncated": true, "_bytes": <serialised size after redaction>}` instead; an object carrying `_truncated` must be exactly that marker. Top-level `_truncated` / `_bytes` are reserved for the marker: caller-owned keys of those names are renamed to `_truncated_user` / `_bytes_user`, with a further `_user` appended while the name is taken (CONTRACT.md §4).

error.description: An error observed by the SDK outside a normal request result.

reason.description: Why authentication or authorisation failed (contract 1.1.0): `missing` no credential was presented, `invalid` it did not verify, `expired` it verified but was past its lifetime, `revoked` it was withdrawn, `scope` it verified but lacked the required scope, `other` the server classified it as none of these. Optional, and set only on `where: auth`, which the schema enforces.

then.description: `reason` classifies an auth failure, so it belongs only to `where: auth`.

custom.description: An application-defined event from `signals.event()`. `props` is capped at 8 KB (8192 bytes) serialised; enforced by collectors as `too_large`.

props.description: Application properties, redacted with the shared key policy (recursive). At most 8 KB (8192 bytes) serialised; enforced by collectors as `too_large`. When still over the cap after redaction the SDK sends the `truncated_object` marker `{"_truncated": true, "_bytes": <serialised size after redaction>}` instead; an object carrying `_truncated` must be exactly that marker. Top-level `_truncated` / `_bytes` are reserved for the marker: caller-owned keys of those names are renamed to `_truncated_user` / `_bytes_user`, with a further `_user` appended while the name is taken (CONTRACT.md §4).

sampling.requested.description: A server-to-client `sampling/createMessage` request (contract 1.1.0). Emitted only when `SIGNALS_PROTOCOL_EVENTS` is on (CONTRACT.md §6); every attribute is optional. `ts` is the start of the request and `duration_ms` its length.

model.description: The model the client named in its result, never the request's model preferences; absent when the client sent no result or named none.

stop_reason.description: The `stopReason` the client reported, as it arrived, truncated to 64 code points.

is_error.description: True when the client answered with a JSON-RPC error, or when the request could not be sent.

rejected.description: True when the client refused the request through its own human-in-the-loop policy, including when it delivered that refusal as a JSON-RPC error carrying the MCP sampling specification's user-rejection code (CONTRACT.md §4). A refusal is not a failure, so `is_error` stays false, and the schema rejects an event that reports both (contract 1.1.0, review round 1, B1).

then.description: A refusal is `rejected: true` with `is_error: false`; both true is rejected with reason `schema`.

elicitation.requested.description: A server-to-client `elicitation/create` request (contract 1.1.0). Emitted only when `SIGNALS_PROTOCOL_EVENTS` is on; every attribute is optional. `ts` is the start of the request and `duration_ms` its length, which includes the time the user took to answer.

mode.description: How the server asked: `form` a schema the client renders, `url` a link the client opens.

action.description: What the client answered: `accept`, `decline`, `cancel`, or `error` when the request failed instead of being answered. Never the answer itself: an elicitation response is user data and no part of it is reported.

task.updated.description: A status change of a long-running task the server exposes (contract 1.1.0). Emitted only when `SIGNALS_PROTOCOL_EVENTS` is on; every attribute is optional. One event per observed status change, not one per poll.

task_id.description: The task identifier the server issued, as it arrived, truncated to 128 code points.

status.description: The status as the protocol spells it (for example `working`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`), truncated to 32 code points. Deliberately not an enum: the task status set is still moving, and an SDK must report what it saw rather than drop an unrecognised value.

poll_count.description: How many status polls the client had made for this task when this change was observed.
